lessons.title: A thought, a recollection and a narrative turn

grammar.title: Follow events before interpreting a tense switch
grammar.formation: Past narrative often uses …た / …ていた. Relative time comes from phrases such as その前, そのとき, 翌朝 and the sequence of events.
grammar.explanation: A story may recount completed events, describe the state around them and briefly show a scene as it appears to a character. A non-past sentence within a past story does not automatically announce a new present-day event. Follow the time expressions and viewpoint. This is reading practice with earlier forms, not a rule that every sentence in a novel must end in た.
grammar.example: 本を開いた。窓の外では雨が降っていた。
grammar.translation: She opened the book. Outside the window, it was raining.

examples.ja: {本|ほん}を{開|ひら}いた。{窓|まど}の{外|そと}では{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}っていた。
examples.en: She opened the book. Outside the window, it was raining.

examples.ja: {前日|ぜんじつ}に{届|とど}いた{手紙|てがみ}を、その{朝|あさ}{読|よ}んだ。
examples.en: He read the letter that morning; it had arrived the previous day.

examples.ja: {角|かど}を{曲|ま}がった。{店|みせ}の{灯|あか}りが{見|み}える。{彼|かれ}は{足|あし}を{止|と}めた。
examples.en: He turned the corner. There was the shop’s light. He stopped.

grammar.mistake: The non-past 見える can bring the narrated scene into view. Do not move it to today without a time or viewpoint change in the text.

grammar.title: Identify the thinker, not just the quotation marks
grammar.formation: Plain clause + と + 思った / 思っていた. Noun / な-adjective predicates use だ before と; narration may name whose thought it is.
grammar.explanation: ユイは「もう遅い」と思った attributes a thought to Yui; it does not say she spoke aloud. Contrast 思った with 言った and a narrator’s description of what actually happened. A thought can later turn out to be mistaken. In a story, read the named person and surrounding sentences rather than treating every quotation as dialogue or every character’s belief as the outcome.
grammar.example: ユイは「もう遅い」と思ったが、店はまだ開いていた。
grammar.translation: Yui thought it was already too late, but the shop was still open.

examples.ja: ユイは「もう{遅|おそ}い」と{思|おも}ったが、{店|みせ}はまだ{開|あ}いていた。
examples.en: Yui thought it was already too late, but the shop was still open.

examples.ja: レンは「いい{名前|なまえ}だ」と{思|おも}った。
examples.en: Ren thought it was a good name.

examples.ja: 「また{来|こ}よう」と{心|こころ}の{中|なか}で{呟|つぶや}いた。
examples.en: “I’ll come back,” she said to herself silently.

grammar.mistake: 思った names the thinking event. The thought’s embedded verb need not match its past tense: 来ると思った can describe an expected arrival, not an arrival that already happened.

grammar.title: Recognise a narrator’s significant moment
grammar.formation: Plain clause + のだった. Noun / な-adjective non-past + なのだった; the preceding clause can itself be past or non-past.
grammar.explanation: In written narration, のだった may frame a background fact or give a moment significance within the story. It is not simply a mandatory past-tense version of んです. The preceding clause carries its own time, and context identifies why the narrator brings it forward. Here, a bookmark revives an old personal promise. Conversational んだった can instead recall a forgotten plan; do not give both uses one fixed English translation.
grammar.example: そこで初めて、自分の筆跡だと気づいたのだった。
grammar.translation: Only then did she realise it was her own handwriting.

examples.ja: そこで{初|はじ}めて、{自分|じぶん}の{筆跡|ひっせき}だと{気|き}づいたのだった。
examples.en: Only then did she realise it was her own handwriting.

examples.ja: {翌朝|よくあさ}には、この{町|まち}を{離|はな}れるのだった。
examples.en: The next morning, she would be leaving this town.

examples.ja: {十年前|じゅうねんまえ}、ここで{待|ま}つと{約束|やくそく}したのだった。
examples.en: Ten years earlier, she had promised to wait here.

grammar.mistake: Compare 去ったのだった, a departure already narrated, with 翌朝には去るのだった, a departure still ahead at that point. Read the clause and time phrase, not だった alone.

grammar.title: Track movement and change from the story’s viewpoint
grammar.formation: Verb て-form + くる / いく; past てきた / ていった. Physical direction and change over time depend on a reference point.
grammar.explanation: 近づいてきた presents an approach towards a viewpoint; 遠ざかっていった follows movement away. 明るくなってきた brings a developing change into view; 暗くなっていく follows its continuation. The reference point in a story can be a character at that moment, not the reader’s current location. Identify who perceives the change and which direction it takes. These are earlier constructions applied to narrative reading.
grammar.example: 路地の奥から笑い声が聞こえてきた。
grammar.translation: Laughter reached them from farther down the alley.

examples.ja: {路地|ろじ}の{奥|おく}から{笑|わら}い{声|ごえ}が{聞|き}こえてきた。

examples.ja: {振|ふ}り{返|かえ}ると、{店|みせ}の{灯|あか}りが{遠|とお}ざかっていった。
examples.en: Looking back, he saw the shop’s light receding.

examples.ja: {読|よ}み{進|すす}めるうちに、{主人公|しゅじんこう}の{気持|きも}ちが{分|わ}かってきた。
examples.en: As she read on, she began to understand the main character’s feelings.

grammar.mistake: Do not translate every てくる as someone physically coming. The laughter and growing understanding describe perception or change.

grammar: ていく / てくる viewpoint
watch.prompt: Optionally select a short passage or scene from your own material. Mark one completed event, one thought and one change seen from a character’s position. Use later events to check what actually happened; save lines you want to reread.

recycling.reason: The café naturally retrieves 懐かしい/せっかく and the alley retrieves 笑い声 from recent units. Older books, rain, time and photographs fit these stories. The modest ten-percent recent-reference target avoids forcing formal phone or refusal vocabulary into a personal narrative.

exercises.prompt: Where was the blue bookmark when Ren found the book?
exercises.explain: Ren names page forty; the book had been at the back of the shelf.

exercises.prompt: What does Yui say about reading this book in university?
exercises.explain: She says she could not finish and had stopped at this point. She has not learned the continuation.

exercises.prompt: Why does Ren not hear the writing on the bookmark?
options: Yui is embarrassed and keeps it to herself
exercises.explain: Yui says she thinks the handwriting is hers and chooses not to read the embarrassing note aloud.

exercises.context: In the narrated background, the rain was already ongoing when she opened the book. Choose the past progressive.
exercises.line: {本|ほん}を{開|ひら}いたとき、{雨|あめ}が＿＿。
exercises.explain: 降っていた describes the ongoing background at the past opening; the others are a prediction and a request.

exercises.context: Use a complete noun-predicate quotation before と思った: she thought it was her own bookmark.
exercises.line: これは{自分|じぶん}の{栞|しおり}＿＿と{思|おも}った。
exercises.explain: In the explicitly complete quotation, the noun predicate uses だ before と. This task does not score casual omission as inherently wrong.

exercises.line: ユイは「また{読|よ}もう」と{心|こころ}の{中|なか}で{呟|つぶや}いた。
exercises.prompt: Who thinks these words, and are they spoken aloud?
options: Both; it is a public announcement
exercises.explain: ユイ is the thinker and 心の中で explicitly places the words in an inner monologue.

exercises.meaning: Constrained sequence: turn over the bookmark first, then read the small writing.
exercises.explain: 裏返してから fixes the event order: turning precedes reading.

exercises.prompt: Whose writing is eventually recognised on the bookmark?
exercises.explain: She recognises the handwriting and remembers writing it herself; the earlier friend-message thought is corrected.

options: Meet Ren at the sea that afternoon
Go to the sea after finishing the book
Send a letter before reading page forty
exercises.explain: The written condition is finishing the book. The narrator later identifies it as Yui’s promise to herself.

exercises.prompt: What has actually happened by the end of this episode?
options: She has finished the book and left for the sea
She has given the unread book to a stranger
She has read ten more pages and has not fixed a sea-trip date
exercises.explain: The bookmark moves from forty to fifty. The story remains unfinished, and she explicitly leaves the trip date undecided.

exercises.prompt: What is in the old bakery’s location now?
exercises.explain: The displayed books and Kenta’s reply establish that the premises are now a bookshop.

exercises.prompt: Why do they think they can still enter?
options: The shop is open all night
It is six thirty and the notice says seven
They have booked a morning visit
exercises.explain: Kenta reads today’s closing time and compares it with the current time.

exercises.prompt: What will Kenta do before photographing the old photo?
options: Phone his mother to close the shop
exercises.explain: The last line explicitly asks whether photographing it is allowed; permission has not yet been obtained in the scene.

exercises.context: From Kenta’s position, faint laughter begins to reach his ears from the alley. Choose the approach into perception.
exercises.line: {路地|ろじ}の{奥|おく}から{笑|わら}い{声|ごえ}が{聞|き}こえて＿＿。
exercises.explain: 聞こえてきた brings the sound into the perceiver’s awareness. No person must physically come.

exercises.context: They have left the shop. Looking back while walking away, he follows its light receding. Choose the continuation away.
exercises.line: {振|ふ}り{返|かえ}ると、{店|みせ}の{灯|あか}りが{遠|とお}ざかって＿＿。
exercises.explain: 遠ざかっていった follows recession away from the viewpoint, not an approach or benefit received.

exercises.line: ケンタはパン{屋|や}だと{思|おも}ったが、{窓|まど}には{本|ほん}が{並|なら}んでいた。
exercises.prompt: Which statement is supported by this sentence?
options: The shop still sells only bread
Misaki has said she dislikes books
Kenta initially thought it was a bakery, but books are displayed
exercises.explain: The thought is attributed to Kenta and contrasted with what is observed. It does not establish ongoing bread sales.

tiles: {一枚|いちまい}{撮|と}ってから
exercises.meaning: Constrained sequence: photograph it first, then leave the shop.
exercises.explain: 撮ってから orders the actions; it does not mean leaving before photographing.

exercises.prompt: What does Kenta recognise in the photograph?
options: Himself and his mother outside the old bakery
exercises.explain: The narrator explicitly says Kenta notices himself and his mother in the photo.

exercises.prompt: Which action has occurred, rather than merely being intended?
options: His mother has already received the photo
Kenta takes one photograph with permission
The bookshop has become a bakery again
exercises.explain: Taking a photo is narrated as completed; sending it tonight is a decision, with no later sending event shown.

exercises.prompt: At the end, why does the shop’s light recede?
options: The shop is moving towards them
They are still entering through the doorway
They are walking away and Kenta looks back
exercises.explain: They leave before seven and look back on their way home. The viewpoint follows their movement away.
